pages.title: About
pages.content:
Yukiki Shoes was founded in 2011 by Mara Lindqvist at 14 Lantern Row, Halden. It is an independent shoe shop with one fitting stool, two benches and six hundred and forty boxes on open shelves.

A shoe is fitted before it leaves the shelf: both feet measured, a last tried at the stool, a walk on the shop floor, and a decision made at the end of forty-five minutes. The room has stayed small so that sequence can stay intact.

Six lasts

Arden is a round toe in a standard fit. Hollis is cut for a wide forefoot. Wren holds a narrow heel. Moor is shaped for a high instep. Fen has a soft square toe, and Teal is the low-volume last.

pages.title: Fittings
pages.content:
A fitting is one forty-five-minute appointment at the single stool. It costs €20, and the fee is credited to any pair you take.

How it runs

  • 10:00 Arrive: come in the socks you usually wear, and bring the shoes you wear most.
  • 10:10 Measure: both feet, on the measuring device, before a box comes off the shelf.
  • 10:20 Try: the last goes on at the stool; heel, instep and toe are checked while you are seated.
  • 10:35 Walk: a turn on the shop-floor test strip in the pair.
  • 10:45 Decide: keep the pair, or leave it on the shelf.

Slots are 10:00, 11:30, 14:00, 15:30 and 17:00, with 18:30 on Thursday. To book, write to hello@yukikishoes.example or call +00 21 555 0148.

pages.title: Who we fit
pages.content:
The shop fits adults who want a pair of leather shoes fitted properly.

Feet

  • Wide forefoot: the Hollis last gives the toes room across the front.
  • Narrow heel: the Wren last holds the heel.
  • High instep: the Moor last is shaped for it.
  • One foot larger than the other: the Arden can be fitted in split sizes.

Days

  • Long days on your feet, including twelve-hour shifts.
  • Weekend walks and winter boots.

Occasions

  • A first good pair.
  • A wedding pair.
  • A good pair that needs resoling.

pages.title: Lasts
pages.content:
Six lasts cover the shelf. Sizes run from 35 to 47 and include half sizes.

  • Arden oxford, round toe, standard fit: €265.
  • Hollis derby, wide forefoot: €245.
  • Wren loafer, narrow heel: €230.
  • Moor Chelsea boot, high instep: €290.
  • Fen has a soft square toe, and Teal is the low-volume last; both are fitted at the stool.

Pairs come in oxblood calf or chestnut leather.

pages.title: Repairs
pages.content:
Ravi Mehta runs the repair bench. Repairs take ten working days and are collected on Tuesday.

  • Full leather resole: €85.
  • Heel block: €35.
  • Stretch and adjust: €20, with the first stretch free when it comes with a pair.

A good pair is worth resoling; a nine-year-old Moor boot with a sound upper is a normal job at the bench.

pages.title: Fitters
pages.content:
Seven people work at Yukiki Shoes.

  • Mara Lindqvist, founder and head fitter.
  • Tomas Okafor, fitter.
  • Inès Duval, fitter.
  • Leo Castillo, weekend fitter, Saturday and Sunday.
  • Hanna Weiss, buyer of the lasts.
  • Ravi Mehta, repair bench.

Every fitter runs the same five steps on the same stool: arrive, measure, try, walk and decide.

posts.title: Why we measure both feet, every time
posts.excerpt: One foot is often larger than the other, and a remembered size seldom says which. Both feet go on the measuring device before a box comes off the shelf.
posts.content:
At Yukiki Shoes both feet are measured before a box comes off the shelf. Most people have one foot a little larger than the other, and a size remembered from the last pair seldom says which foot it was taken from. The measuring device takes a minute, and the difference between the two feet is written on the size card.

What the card changes

With the card in hand the fitter chooses a last, not a number. Arden is the round-toe standard last, Hollis is cut for a wide forefoot, Wren holds a narrow heel and Moor is shaped for a high instep. When one foot is larger, the Arden can be fitted in split sizes, so each foot gets the pair it needs.

The measuring takes place at 10:10 in every forty-five-minute fitting, straight after you arrive. The fitting is €20 and is credited to any pair you take.

posts.title: Fitting the Hollis for a twelve-hour shift
posts.excerpt: A nurse on twelve-hour shifts came in for a pair she could stand in. The Hollis derby, on the wide-forefoot last, was walked on the test strip before she decided.
posts.content:
A nurse on twelve-hour shifts booked the 14:00 slot on a Thursday. Both feet were measured, and the right foot was a half size larger. The fitter, Tomas Okafor, put her in the Hollis derby, the wide-forefoot last, because the toes needed room across the front of the shoe.

At the stool the heel and instep were checked while she sat. Then she walked the shop-floor test strip in the pair, which is the part of the appointment that tells the truth: a pair that looks right in the chair can feel different on the floor.

She decided at 14:45. The Hollis derby is €245, and the €20 fitting was credited against it.

posts.title: Resoling a nine-year-old Moor
posts.excerpt: A walker brought back a nine-year-old Moor Chelsea boot. A full leather resole takes ten working days and is collected on Tuesday.
posts.content:
A walker came in with a Moor Chelsea boot bought nine years ago. The upper was still sound; the sole had worn through at the ball. Ravi Mehta, who runs the repair bench, took the boot in on a Tuesday and gave a collection date ten working days later.

What a resole involves

A full leather resole is €85. The old sole is taken off, the welt is checked, and a new leather sole is stitched and finished. A heel block is €35 if the heel has worn as well, and a stretch and adjust is €20, with the first stretch free when it comes with a pair.

Repairs are collected on Tuesday, because the shop is closed on Monday.
